items.streamTitle: Open Stroop, fNIRS and VR-cycling dataset enabled linked attention measurements
items.streamSummary: A November 11 Scientific Data release provides synchronized Stroop, fNIRS and physiological records from 42 randomized young adults around VR versus ordinary cycling and control. It is an enabling dataset, not proven XR training efficacy.
items.attribution: Li and Yang — Scientific Data (open multimodal XR/attention dataset, November 11)

items.streamTitle: Translation-enabled scoring extracted autobiographical detail from German narratives
items.streamSummary: A study of 1,920 German autobiographical narratives found translation-to-English enabled automated internal/external detail scoring with little observed degradation against manual ratings. Cross-cultural field transfer needs validation.
items.attribution: Groer, Külpmann, Zlomuzica and Plank — Scientific Reports (multilingual narrative measurement, November 10)

items.streamTitle: Privacy concerns conditioned Gen Z trust in AI-mediated commerce
items.streamSummary: A 979-student Chinese survey linked AI transparency, peer recommendations and usability to trust and purchase intention, with privacy-related moderation. All pathways are observational.
items.attribution: Ma and Zheng — Scientific Reports (cross-sectional Gen Z consumer survey, November 10)

items.streamTitle: Corporate AI rhetoric correlated with longer audit delays, with institutional differences
items.streamSummary: An archival study of 31,389 Chinese firm-years linked AI-focused disclosure to longer audit delays; some auditor and regulatory contexts moderated the association. It is not causal evidence of individual auditor cognition.
items.attribution: Huang — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (firm-level archival study, November 10)

items.streamTitle: Long-term motor learning became more stable and specialized over fifteen weeks
items.streamSummary: Repeated force-field reaching practice in 28 adults produced stronger retention and more specialized responses over weeks. It supports testing delayed skill retention, not assuming cognitive-training transfer.
items.attribution: Franklin, Nietschmann and Franklin — Nature Human Behaviour (motor-learning experiments, November 9)

items.streamTitle: Persistent agent correction rules improved compliance in a controlled benchmark
items.streamSummary: Decision Context converted agent corrections into scoped rules and reported about 95% benchmark compliance versus 55% for naive retrieval. Mocked tool traces limit claims about deployed research reliability.
items.attribution: Vahdat and Vaezipoor — arXiv preprint (agent-memory benchmark, November 5)

items.streamTitle: LLM judges agreed with each other more than with human counterspeech experts
items.streamSummary: Twelve open LLMs showed low agreement with human experts when rating counterspeech, even where model-to-model agreement was strong. Automatic scoring needs human benchmarking and is not evidence of intervention effectiveness.
items.attribution: Alali, Ocampo and Ceolin — arXiv preprint (counterspeech-judge evaluation, November 3)

items.streamTitle: Chaotic systems exposed fragility of long-horizon counterfactual predictions
items.streamSummary: Formal counterfactual simulations showed that small uncertainties can amplify dramatically in chaotic dynamics despite adequate factual fit. This cautions long-horizon COA modeling; human-system applicability is untested.
items.attribution: Aalaila, Großmann, Mukherjee et al. — Scientific Reports (formal counterfactual simulation study, June 2)

items.streamTitle: Cognitive-map experiments separated stable knowledge from goal-focused representations
items.streamSummary: Human fMRI and recurrent-network analyses found stable multidimensional cognitive maps in memory-related networks but flexible goal-relevant representations in frontoparietal regions. Neural-model similarity is not direct proof of an identical human algorithm.
items.attribution: Park, Zolfaghar, Russin et al. — Nature Communications (human fMRI and recurrent-network study, November 10)

items.streamTitle: Neural representations of evidence and reward predicted different causal effects on choices
items.streamSummary: Recordings and causal microstimulation in two rhesus monkeys found distinct choice effects from sensory and frontal populations despite both encoding motion and reward. The result is task-specific neural evidence, not an operational human model.
items.attribution: Ruff, Markman, Kim and Cohen — Nature Neuroscience (primate neural recordings, modeling and stimulation, November 10)

items.streamTitle: Global information-regulation dataset tracked a shift from broad bans to targeted harms
items.streamSummary: A 409-entry international policy dataset found accelerating misinformation regulation and a shift toward specific harms and platform duties. Counts document legislative activity, not effectiveness or behavioral impact.
items.attribution: Abbas, Chesterman and Putra — arXiv report, Beyond Falsehoods 2026 (global regulatory dataset)

items.streamTitle: Historical records reveal generational shifts in perceived climate extremes
items.streamSummary: Four centuries of northern Chinese archives diverged systematically from natural climate proxies; 20–40-year moving baselines improved agreement. A heuristic simulation supports but cannot prove generational-memory explanations.
items.attribution: Song, Hu, Findley et al. — Nature Communications (historical archival analysis and simulation, November 9)

items.streamTitle: PRISMA review-agent pipeline exposed retrieval, bookkeeping and oversight gaps
items.streamSummary: PARIS orchestrated 15 agents through two review case studies, but audits found missing retrieval, drifting record counts and unrecorded checkpoints; only 8/27 PRISMA items were fully supported and review quality lacked independent evaluation.
items.attribution: Cruz, Ghanem, Jabbar, Ait Kbir and Cherifi — arXiv preprint, PARIS (multi-agent evidence-synthesis case studies)

items.streamTitle: ShopMind improved synthetic shopping predictions by modeling changing inferred mental states
items.streamSummary: ShopMind used evolving simulated beliefs and intentions to improve reported personalization and behavioral realism in shopping-task benchmarks. Synthetic internal states are not independently verified human mental states.
items.attribution: Hou, Chen, He, Xu, Ma and Song — arXiv preprint, ShopMind (behavioral simulation benchmark)

items.streamTitle: New mediation estimators separated individual and peer pathways under interference
items.streamSummary: A semiparametric framework decomposes intervention mediation into own-person and peer-spillover components despite treatment-induced confounding. Mathematical and simulation results do not establish validity in untested influence studies.
items.attribution: Ham, Cheng and Li — arXiv preprint (causal mediation methods, November 9)

items.streamTitle: EU investigators described opportunistic foreign amplification of French unrest
items.streamSummary: Reuters reported EU and French assessments of foreign-aligned accounts exploiting French unrest with fabricated narratives. Investigators found no evidence these actors caused the protests; engagement figures do not establish persuasion.
items.attribution: Reuters — November 9 original reporting on internal EU and French government assessments

items.streamTitle: Synthetic populations lost temporal validity despite sophisticated generation methods
items.streamSummary: Multi-year evaluations found synthetic agent populations lose representativeness; ideal future-informed static projection worked best but was impractical, while aggregate-based updates failed to preserve some attribute dependencies.
items.attribution: Darsel, Côme, Rich, Pereira and Oukhellou — arXiv preprint (synthetic-population forecasting comparison)

items.streamTitle: WorkflowArena tested whether AI agents can design and execute useful team structures
items.streamSummary: WorkflowArena scored 145 integrated professional tasks across nine models and found domain-dependent orchestration behavior; workflow design sometimes improved fixed weaker executors. Real research validity was not established.
items.attribution: Jiang et al. — arXiv preprint, WorkflowArena (verified multi-agent workflow benchmark)

items.streamTitle: EU launched a pilot public repository of political-ad provenance and targeting disclosures
items.streamSummary: The European Commission opened a voluntary pilot repository for political-ad disclosure on October 12. It enables structured sponsor and targeting records in principle but is not yet evidence of full coverage, enforcement or behavioral effects.
items.attribution: European Commission, Directorate-General for Communication — official pilot infrastructure announcement (October 12)

items.streamTitle: A new commentary treats AI slop as a community judgment, not merely a detection label
items.streamSummary: A November 9 Nature Human Behaviour Comment reframes AI slop as context-dependent unwanted content judged by communities, not synonymous with AI origin. It is conceptual, not an evaluated moderation intervention.
items.attribution: So et al. — Nature Human Behaviour (Comment)

items.streamTitle: Culture shapes episodic remembering across personal, legal and political contexts
items.streamSummary: A November 9 Nature Reviews Psychology review argues that culture shapes episodic remembering and interpersonal reconstruction, with legal and political applications. It synthesizes prior evidence; it is not a new causal experiment.
items.attribution: Wang, Jobson, Mert and Vredeveldt — Nature Reviews Psychology (research review)

items.streamTitle: Synthetic advertising personas performed better with fewer demographic details
items.streamSummary: A November 6 preprint benchmarked simulated ad audiences against campaign records across five demographic segments. Leaner persona signals produced lower prediction error than richer prompts; validation outside the campaign remains open.
items.attribution: Choi, Lee, Seo, Lee and Choi — arXiv preprint (real-campaign synthetic-persona benchmark)

items.streamTitle: An LLM simulation replication changed dramatically after one overlooked instruction
items.streamSummary: ODD+LLM shows that one missed role instruction materially changed naming-game convergence, while a review of 28 studies found pervasive missing implementation details. It is a reproducibility advance, not human validation.
items.attribution: Downes, Milletich and Hirst — arXiv preprint (ODD+LLM reporting method and replication study)

items.streamTitle: Randomized agent interventions enabled estimation of when human review helps
items.streamSummary: A November 6 preprint estimates dynamic causal effects of randomized verification and steering within AI-agent trajectories; results vary by action and state. Benefits in deployed research workflows remain untested.
items.attribution: Sawarni, Xing, Zrnic, Johari and Syrgkanis — arXiv preprint (causal agent-evaluation framework)
